$comment: Defects found by the Gate 2 checks in the frozen v0.8 baseline. Each needs an owner decision before any visible change (Gate 2 rule). `status` is open until the owner approves a correction. A check reports a known finding as a note and fails on any new or worse one, and on any entry that no longer occurs.

findings.status: accepted (APR-JE-023): Option A adopted as a documentation policy in docs/JADE_AND_EMBER_MEDIA_RIGHTS_POLICY.md; media/PROVENANCE.md deliberately unchanged (frozen); rights remain unverified and are required evidence for any client release
findings.description: media/PROVENANCE.md records how the six images and the hero loop were made (generator, seeds, prompts, post-processing, known defects) but states no licence or rights terms for the generated media. Audit finding m-8.
findings.proposal: Add a short 'Rights and licence' section to media/PROVENANCE.md naming the generator and account terms that apply, and stating that the media is for the fictional demonstration only and must be replaced for a real client. Documentation only: no pixel, word on any page or behaviour changes. The file sits in the frozen media/ folder and in the preview package, so changing it is a change to the frozen baseline's files and needs owner approval; it would also need an allowlist entry for the media-bytes comparison.

findings.status: accepted (APR-JE-023) as a documented limitation: harmless console messages over file://
findings.description: When index.html is opened straight from the folder (file://), Chromium logs up to 6 console messages per page load about the two <link rel="preload" as="font" crossorigin> tags: the preload fetch is a CORS request from the opaque origin "null" and is refused, and the unused-preload warning follows. The fonts themselves load normally from the stylesheet (all four web fonts report loaded, nothing differs on screen, and every functional check passes). Over http and https there is no message. Present since v0.8 (the same messages appear for the frozen baseline). Firefox and Safari behaviour over file:// is untested here.
findings.proposal: Recommended: accept it. It is console noise in one delivery mode, it hides nothing, and removing the preloads would delay the web fonts on every HTTP visit (a possible visible flash of the metric-matched fallback fonts, which would be a visual change). If the owner wants a silent console over file://, the two preload tags can be emitted only for HTTP builds through a build option (a new build flag, no change to the default pages); that changes the HTML bytes of the HTTP build and needs an allowlist entry and a visual re-check. Not applied.

findings.status: open: awaiting owner decision (recommended: leave as is)
findings.description: html-validate's tel-non-breaking rule reports 6 phone numbers across the five pages (header, visit, order and footer occurrences) written with ordinary spaces and hyphens, "(555) 010-0188". On a narrow screen the number could break across two lines. The same markup is in the frozen v0.8 baseline. The rule is switched off in htmlvalidate.json and measured here so the count cannot grow unnoticed.
findings.proposal: Recommended: leave it. Replacing the spaces and hyphens with non-breaking characters is a typographic change to the visible text of every page and to the v0.8 page bytes (it would need an allowlist entry, a visual re-check and owner approval). The 320 px reflow check shows no clipped or overlapping number today. If approved, the build could emit the non-breaking form for client builds only (the demonstration stays byte-identical). Not applied.
